To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
stainless steel nanospraying provides the highest overall ion intensity and sensitivity, but the resulting data were the least reproducible.

the stainless steel nanospary needle provides the greatest overall sensitivity, the lowest‐flow electrospray source provides the most reproducible protein identifications and the coated glass Picotips provide the highest quality peptide fragmentation spectra.

the stainless steel nanospary needle provides the highest sensitivity, but the most variable data, whereas the low flow source provides the most reproducible data, but at a lower level of sensitivity.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of an ESI source that is compatible with high‐flow monolithic columns and that is capable of generating high‐quality data in terms of the number of protein identifications and the number of high‐quality fragmentation spectra.
the performance of five different EIS sources coupled to monolithic column LC‐MS and MS/MS.
the performance of different electrospray sources, in conjunction with monolithic column liquid‐chromatography, in the analysis of complex protein mixtures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the performance of the ESI source is dependent upon the application and the nature of the sample.
the stainless steel nanoflow sprayer is the best source for the analysis of complex protein mixtures, while the Picotip is best suited to the analysis of simple protein mixtures.
the stainless steel nanosprray needle provides the highest‐quality data, while the coated glass Picotips provide the highest sensitivity and reproducibility.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the stainless steel nanospary source is a good choice for the identification of proteins of high abundance, but for the identification of low abundance proteins the standard ESI source would be the preferred option.

a stainless steel nanospary needle is a good choice for high sensitivity and reproducibility in terms of protein identifications, but a coated glass Picospray tip is preferable in terms of the overall data quality and number of proteins identified in a single analysis.
a stainless steel nanosprray needle provides a high‐quality data set for a complex mixture of proteins, but that a low‐flow source provides a more reproducible data set.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of a stainless steel nanospary source in conjunction with a rapid monolithic column provides an effective means of increasing sensitivity in LC‐MS/MS analysis of complex protein mixtures.
the use of nanospray needles in conjunction with a monolithic column is a viable alternative to conventional ESI sources, providing a significant improvement in sensitivity.
a nanospray needle is the best choice of source for high‐throughput LC‐ESI MS/MS analyses, but it is not the only choice.
